```{r setup}
library(consensusR)
```

This vignette covers two things that aren't obvious from the function
reference alone: exactly what shape the returned data is in, and how to wire
this package into an LLM agent - since that is expected to be one of the
main ways this package gets used, not a secondary use case.

## Searching

```{r}
consensus_search(
  "Does creatine improve cognition?",
  year_min = 2015,
  study_types = c("rct", "meta-analysis")
)
```

`study_types` and `domain` are validated **locally**, against
[consensus_study_types()] and [consensus_domains()], before any request is
sent. An invalid value raises an immediate error that lists every valid
option, rather than a 422 from the API:

```{r}
consensus_search("x", study_types = "not_a_real_type")
#> Error:
#> ! Invalid value for `study_types`: "not_a_real_type".
#> i Valid values are: "bench experiment", "case report", ..., "animal".
```

This matters more for this package than for a typical API wrapper: a human
calling this interactively will typically copy a value from documentation,
but a value chosen by an LLM agent from a natural-language prompt is far more
likely to be a close-but-wrong guess (e.g. `"randomized controlled trial"`
instead of `"rct"`). Local validation turns that into a fast, actionable
error instead of a round trip to the API.

`consensus_search()` returns one page (20 results by default, up to 1000 via
`page_size`). `consensus_search_all()` follows pagination automatically,
pausing one second between requests to respect the API's documented rate
limit, and returns every page combined into one tibble:

```{r}
consensus_search_all(
  "Does creatine improve cognition?",
  study_types = c("rct", "meta-analysis"),
  max_pages = 5
)
```

## Output format

Both functions return a `tibble`, one row per paper. The exact columns
present can vary slightly between papers (a field the API has nothing to
report simply isn't in that paper's JSON object, and becomes `NA` after
row-binding), but as of this package's last verification against the live
API, a result looks like this:

```
# A tibble: 5 x 22
  title    abstract doi   journal_name pages publish_year url   volume
  <chr>    <chr>    <chr> <chr>        <chr>        <int> <chr> <chr>
  ...
# i 14 more variables: citation_count <int>, study_type <chr>,
#   takeaway <chr>, publisher_name <chr>, sjr_best_quartile <int>,
#   study_count <int>, is_preprint <lgl>, countries_of_study <list>,
#   study_duration_days <int>, influential_citation_count <int>,
#   institutions <list>, publish_date <chr>, authors <list>,
#   authors_str <chr>, semantic_score <dbl>, full_text_chunks <list>
```

**Reliable on every normal result:** `title`, `abstract`, `doi`, `url`,
`journal_name`, `publisher_name`, `volume`, `pages`, `publish_year`,
`publish_date`, `citation_count`, `influential_citation_count`,
`study_type`, `is_preprint`, `takeaway`.

**Present only when the API has the data for that paper (`NA` otherwise):**
`sjr_best_quartile`, `sample_size`, `study_count`, `study_duration_days`,
`population_type`. Do not assume these are populated - a `sample_size` of
`NA` means "not reported by the API," not "zero."

**List-columns**, because each paper has a variable number of entries:
`authors`, `countries_of_study`, `institutions`, and (only when
`include_full_text_chunks = TRUE` and the paper's full text is licensed on
your plan) `full_text_chunks`. Unnest one with `tidyr::unnest()`:

```{r}
result <- consensus_search("statins and cardiovascular risk", page_size = 5)
tidyr::unnest(result, authors) # one row per (paper, author) pair
```

`authors_str` is `authors` collapsed into a single `"; "`-separated string,
added specifically because list-columns don't print in a `gt`/`knitr` table
and are awkward for an LLM to reason about compared to a flat string. Prefer
`authors_str` for display and for anything you hand to a model; keep
`authors` for programmatic per-author work.

`takeaway` is a short, AI-generated plain-language summary of the paper's
finding - convenient for a quick scan or a dashboard tile, but it is a
*generated summary*, not a verbatim quote. Verify it against `abstract` (or
`full_text_chunks`, where licensed) before treating it as a citable claim in
a report.

Pagination metadata (`page`, `page_size`, `is_end`, `next_page`) is attached
as **attributes** on the returned tibble, not extra columns:

```{r}
attr(result, "is_end")
attr(result, "next_page")
```

### Building an evidence table

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

consensus_search(
  "statins and cardiovascular risk",
  study_types = c("rct", "meta-analysis"),
  page_size = 10
) |>
  select(title, authors_str, journal_name, publish_year, study_type, citation_count, takeaway) |>
  arrange(desc(citation_count)) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Evidence summary: statins and cardiovascular risk")
```

## For LLM agents

This package is expected to be called by LLM agents at least as often as by
a human analyst writing a script - so "how an agent should search, and how
it should read the result" is specified here explicitly, not left to be
inferred from the general function reference.

### Preferred path: `consensus_search_tool()`

If your agent framework is [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org), register
the ready-made tool rather than hand-wrapping `consensus_search()`:

```{r}
chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic()
chat$register_tool(consensus_search_tool())
chat$chat("Does creatine improve cognition? Cite RCTs or meta-analyses.")
```

This tool:

- Declares `study_types` and `domain` as **enums** in the schema the model
  sees (sourced from [consensus_study_types()] / [consensus_domains()]), so
  a well-behaved model is constrained to valid values before it ever calls
  the tool, rather than discovering the constraint from an error.
- Returns a **flat list of records** - one list per paper, containing only
  scalar fields (`title`, `authors_str`, `journal_name`, `publish_year`,
  `doi`, `url`, `study_type`, `sample_size`, `citation_count`, `takeaway`,
  `abstract`). List-columns (`authors`, `countries_of_study`,
  `institutions`, `full_text_chunks`) and pagination attributes are
  deliberately dropped here, because this is the representation the model
  actually reads as tool output (serialized to text/JSON), and a flat list
  of records is far more reliable for a model to parse and cite from than a
  tibble with list-columns.
- Defaults `page_size` to 10, not 20 - every extra result costs tokens in
  the model's context window. Raise it only if you specifically want the
  agent to see more candidates per search.

### Building your own wrapper instead

If you're integrating with a different agent framework, replicate this same
contract rather than inventing a new one:

1. Constrain `study_types` to [consensus_study_types()] and `domain` to
   [consensus_domains()] in whatever schema format your framework uses.
2. Return scalar fields only (see the list above) - drop list-columns and
   pagination attributes before handing results to the model.
3. Keep `page_size` small (10-20) by default for the same token-budget
   reason.
4. If your agent will present `takeaway` as a finding, have it (or your
   prompt) also check `abstract` - `takeaway` is generated text, and an
   agent repeating it as a direct quote without that check can
   misrepresent the source.

## Rate limits

The Consensus API documents a limit of roughly one request per second on
standard plans. `consensus_search_all()` and `consensus_search_tool()`'s
single-call-per-turn design both respect this without extra effort on your
part; if you're issuing many individual `consensus_search()` calls in a
loop (e.g. one per item in a batch job), add `Sys.sleep(1)` between calls
yourself.
